parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime shows no criminalisation of trans identity or expression, and courts have affirmatively protected trans people (2023 marker ruling, July 2025 toilet ruling striking down facility exclusion). Against this: no anti-discrimination or hate-crime statute, so street-level recourse for the reported physical/sexual toilet abuse is thin; institutional resistance and ~80% opposition to partnership legislation signal real social hostility; the 2013 border customs sexual abuse is documented but dated and single; visitor document handling at entry is an open question. Severity if outed is moderate (harassment, service friction, thin recourse) rather than custodial. This sits below the 0.65 friction-with-working-remedies tier because remedies for everyday hostility are undocumented, above 0.55 because courts demonstrably function for trans claimants.

entry_documents.exposure: 2013: trans woman subjected to 9-hour invasive customs search, sexual abuse, left stateless. April 2024 surgical criteria govern local marker changes; dossier does not state whether foreign-issued markers are questioned at entry.
entry_documents.protection: Cross-dressing not illegal; no documented current policy screening visitors' gender markers. Courts have ruled against document-based exclusion (Feb 2023).
entry_documents.interaction: Document/marker mismatch could route a visitor into customs handling resembling the 2013 case; unknown whether that pathway persists.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: The 2013 customs abuse involved prolonged involuntary search/detention by officers. No documented arrests for trans identity or presentation.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No criminalisation of cross-dressing; no documented custody placement rules for visitors; courts have provided relief in rights cases.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If a visitor is detained, thin statutory recourse (no hate-crime law) limits complaint channels, though constitutional litigation has worked for residents.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Trans people report verbal, physical and sexual abuse in public toilets — a universal-exposure setting. No standing subnational variation documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 23 July 2025 high court ruled the toilet ban unconstitutional under equality — an operative, recent ruling.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Ruling's scope (government vs private venues), implementation and complaints mechanism are not described, so the protective effect on a visitor's daily use is uncertain.

care_services.exposure: 2025 report found LGBTQ exclusion across health domains. No anti-discrimination statute to remedy a visitor refused care.
care_services.protection: No documented care denial to visitors; partner medical-decision rights exist in part but same-sex partnership bill was rejected (Sept 2025), leaving gaps for a visitor with a partner.
care_services.interaction: An injured or ill outed visitor enters a system with documented exclusion and no statutory non-discrimination hook; recourse would require constitutional litigation, not a fast remedy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Institutional resistance episodes (banned airline ad, broadcaster ruling) and conservative/religious political opposition frame LGBT visibility as a threat; 80% of submissions opposed partnership bill.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Courts repeatedly rule for LGBT claimants (2006 age-consent precedent, 2018 spousal visas, 2023, 2024, 2025 rulings); cross-dressing lawful.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing is mixed: judiciary protective, legislature and regulators resistant — a visitor's exposure depends on which actor she meets.

minors_guardians.exposure: Same surgical/hormonal ID criteria apply to trans youth locally; 2025 report notes exclusion in education. No documented rule governing a visiting trans minor's documents or facilities.
minors_guardians.protection: First-instance custody/step-child adoption precedents for same-sex couples (2021); guardianship ordinance gives courts full control.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family's exposure at school visits, facilities or document checks for a minor is not documented either way.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Reported physical and sexual abuse in public toilets; 2025 report flags personal-security exclusion; no hate-crime legislation means no disaggregated figures or bias-enhanced penalties.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Constitutional equality right has produced facility-access relief (July 2025); cross-dressing lawful; no documented pattern of police targeting trans visitors.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A visitor assaulted street-level faces thin statutory recourse; police response quality for trans victims is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law, no hate-crime law, no incident counts; partnership bill rejected Sept 2025; 2023 direction to create recognition framework within two years appears unfulfilled.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts with a track record of pro-trans rulings (2018, 2023, 2024, 2025); spousal visas, joint tax, housing equality all court-ordered and in force.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy exists at constitutional level but is slow and litigation-dependent — impractical for a short-stay visitor facing street friction.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: no entry ban, register, or universal exclusion of trans visitors exists here; courts affirmatively protect facility access. The dossier documents friction and thin recourse, not systematic border exclusion with no remedy.

Higher than 0.55-B: there is no discretionary secondary-screening or refused-admission regime documented against trans visitors, and courts have ruled for trans claimants repeatedly. The dated 2013 customs abuse is a single past event, not a routine screening practice.

Below 0.75-C: that anchor has trained border officers, a tribunal granting detention appeals, and compensation for unlawful holding. Here visitor document handling is undocumented, there is no anti-discrimination or hate-crime statute, and reported toilet abuse lacks a shown complaints mechanism.

parsed.synthesis: The regime is judicially protective but statutorily thin: courts have struck down facility exclusion (July 2023-2025 line), ordered spousal visas, housing equality, and barred full-surgery prerequisites — genuine, operative protections. Against that, no anti-discrimination or hate-crime law leaves street-level abuse (reported physical/sexual toilet incidents) with thin recourse; institutional and legislative resistance plus ~80% opposition to partnership recognition show real social hostility alongside documented generational acceptance. The 2013 border sexual abuse is severe but dated and single. Visitor document handling at entry is an open question, not a documented exposure. For an adult alone, daily exposure is harassment and service friction with slow constitutional remedies; for a travelling family, minor-specific rules are not documented. Net: Elevated-to-Reduced Risk, weighted below working-remedy tiers because everyday recourse is unshown.
